small_guidance:
- The current gather kernel iterates all KD*KH*KW=27 taps per output but only ~1/8 are valid (stride=2). Restructure by computing tap validity from `(od+PD) % SD` etc. once per output and only iterating the single valid (kd,kh,kw) per spatial axis — i.e. derive `kd = (od+PD) % SD`, `id_ = (od+PD)//SD`, dropping the outer static loops over kd/kh/kw and just looping over valid taps (1 per axis when in range). This cuts dot calls by ~8×.
- Add larger autotune configs targeting the GEMM shape (OC=128, IC=64 → small K): try `BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_SP=64, IC_TILE=64` (full IC in one tile, removes inner ic loop), and `BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP=256, IC_TILE=64` with num_warps=8, num_stages=2-4.
- Cache the reordered weight as `(OC, KD*KH*KW*IC)` so the per-tap K dimension can be flattened into one GEMM-K loop, eliminating the per-tap dot overhead and letting Triton pipeline the K loop.
large_guidance:
- Switch from gather to scatter-add: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)` computes `x[n, ic, id, ih, iw] · W[ic, :, kd, kh, kw]` outer product and `tl.atomic_add`s into the output grid at `(od=id*SD-PD+kd, ...)`. For ConvTranspose3d with stride=2 this matches the natural data flow — each input contributes to exactly KD*KH*KW=27 output points — and avoids the wasted 7/8 zero-tap work the gather form does.
- Alternatively, since stride=2 means each output position `(od,oh,ow)` is touched by exactly one `(kd,kh,kw)` determined by parity, write a parity-specialized gather: 8 sub-kernels (or a single kernel keyed on `(od%2, oh%2, ow%2)`) each doing a pure GEMM with K=IC (no kernel-tap loop, no validity mask on taps). This collapses the conv-transpose to 8 plain GEMMs of shape (OC, IC) × (IC, sub-volume).
- Fuse the bias+clamp+divide epilogue (already done) and ensure the output store uses channels-last-style coalescing on the OW axis; consider persistent-CTA over the spatial tile so weight tiles stay in registers across multiple output tiles for the same OC block.
